items.name: Sequence as the engine of continuation
items.description: A one- or two-bar figure is restated a step lower (occasionally a step higher) two or three times, usually over a circle-of-fifths bass. This is how a Corelli phrase gets from its opening to its caden

items.name: The suspension chain
items.description: Consecutive 7–6 or 4–3 suspensions between the two upper parts, each resolution preparing the next dissonance. Often welded onto the sequence above, so harmony and dissonance drive forward together.

items.name: A walking bass that is a real line
items.description: The bass moves in steady crotchets or quavers with its own contour and its own cadences, not as chord roots. Under the sequences it walks by fifths; under the cadences it steps.

items.name: Two equal upper voices crossing and exchanging
items.description: The trio-sonata texture: the violins are peers, trade the leading part, cross freely, and move in parallel thirds and sixths for long stretches. Neither is an accompaniment to the other.

items.name: Clear, unhurried cadential punctuation
items.description: Phrases end in unambiguous perfect or half cadences with a 4–3 suspension in the penultimate chord, and the harmonic rhythm broadens as they approach. The form is audible because the cadences are.
